corrections: 2026-09-27: first pass described the 27 blob names as 'embedded model weights'. That was wrong - they are shader labels. Corrected after counting 5,176 DXIL/DXBC containers covering ~50 MB of the 63 MB .rdata.

composition_analysis.note: Approximate. The unexplained remainder is the candidate weight region; it is contiguous enough to hold an FSR4 v07 FP8 network but has not been parsed into named tensors with shapes.

identification.embedded_model_blobs_note: The 27 distinct fsr4_model_v07_* names are DXBC/DXIL shader debug labels, one per compiled shader variant, not a weight table. They were initially mis-read as a model manifest; container analysis corrected this.
identification.precision_of_embedded_model: FP8 ('no_scale'); an 'FSR4-i8' INT8 code path also exists in the binary
identification.product: AMD FidelityFX FSR4 upscaler runtime, model revision v07
identification.vendor: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (version resource strings)

purpose: Identify an externally supplied binary BEFORE any use. An inventory is not licence clearance and not permission to execute.

status.weights_located: approximately 13 MB region in .rdata, not yet parsed

what_this_does_NOT_unblock: It is a Windows x86-64 DLL. It cannot execute on Apple Silicon and cannot be loaded into Metal.
Portability requires the model weights and graph to be re-expressed in Metal; the DX12 code path itself is dead on this platform.
AMD's FSR4 licence does not grant redistribution or reimplementation rights. The embedded weights are AMD's intellectual property.
Extraction and reuse of the weights is a licensing decision, not a technical one, and has not been cleared.
what_this_unblocks: The FSR4 v07 network topology is recoverable: 13 sequential 'pass' blocks with pre/post variants, plus prepass/postpass.
Real FSR4 weights are embedded in the binary rather than shipped as a separate public file.
G0 provenance for FSR4 can be investigated with a concrete artifact instead of a blocked download.
